reaction: A caretaker with a notebook from Rizza... Riza. I like that residents vote on me; people who remember what I did. Continuing the saved notebook as asked.

Recognition guess at 3s: Hacer in flat 1, and Riza left me the notebook. In Voice, Hacer was Halil’s neighbour who stood at the door with him, and Riza was a friend in his goals list. Low-to-moderate confidence; common names. Oh, maybe the same street? I am curious. Before running for bread I want to see all five orders.
Everyone wants bread. Tarık is earliest and farthest up. I hope I can carry more than one loaf at a time; I will go to the bakery and see.

Swap Hacer’s and Sevim’s newspapers? That is a strange little temptation. Do they want each other’s paper, or is it mischief? I do not know them yet, so I will not meddle on day one. Taking Tarık his bread.
He calls me son. And the stairs are hard for him; flat 7 at the top. A conversation menu, finally, with time paused while he talks. Others are waiting for bread, but I want one question first.

His family may ring on Sunday, and he is not sure. That is a little sad and very specific. I want to remember it. Sitting with him is tempting, but the others are waiting for bread, so I will come back.
Good, I seem to be carrying all the bread at once. Hacer next. I want to see whether she is the Hacer I half-remember.
If there is a cat! I love that hedge. Five lira tip. She believes what I say, which feels like a responsibility. What can I tell her? Maybe Tarık’s worry about his family.

I can choose how sure I sound: as I heard it, or for certain. And Make something up! I like that rumour is a tool. I will pass on the water notice honestly, as I heard it, though there are two identical buttons and I hope I am pressing the water one.
Tapping the first as I heard it, beside the water notice.
That is interesting. A bit flat for a water notice, but fine. Asking her what is new.
Her knee predicts rain. I want to see if it does rain; that would be a nice little thing to have noticed. On to Sevim next door.
Sevim next.

Just after sixty-two seconds, written right after a wait returned, so a little late. I am the caretaker carrying the morning bread up and down the stairwell. I chose Continue, looked at all five orders, then went to the bakery and carried everything at once. Tarık told me his family may ring Sunday; Hacer predicted rain with her knee; I told her the water notice as I heard it. Sevim is not sure she can trust me. I like that each door has a little person behind it and conversations pause the clock. The Tell menu had two identical as I heard it buttons, which tripped me. I am curious whether Tarık and Hacer remember what I say.
She is not sure she can trust me. Rather than pass on news, I want to try sitting with her. Burak still needs his bread by 08:25, so I hope this is short.
Oh. A teacher, children reading aloud for forty years, and she still hears them in the evenings. As a library assistant that one goes straight to me. That was worth ten minutes of bread time.
She still says she is not sure she can trust me after we sat. Fair, it is day one. Burak and Derya are waiting.
Burak, the one who posted the water notice.
You have helped me so much, on my first morning, while also not sure he can trust me. That mismatch made me smile; it sounds like a stock thank-you. What is new with him?
He tells me his own notice back. Third time I have read the water line now. Off to Derya with two loaves.
Derya is the only one without in beside her name. I am going anyway; I wonder what happens to bread at an empty door.
Hung the bread on her door handle, a nice concrete image. All bread out before eight-thirty. Now nothing is due, and there is a Skip button, but I would rather read Rıza’s notebook than rush.

Two of sixteen things learned: Hacer sees everyone who passes, Tarık would give me his last lemon candy. I did not learn the candy from anything I read, but I like it. Sevim’s forty years of children reading is not counted, which surprises me; that felt like the biggest thing I learned. Also Derya was out and is now asleep? I will go sit with Tarık.
Derya works night shifts. Ring the bell anyway is offered, but waking a night-shift nurse or whoever she is would be cruel. Going up to Tarık.
A widowed retired ferry captain on the top floor. Now I want to hear about the ferries. Sitting together.
The ferry froze in 1974 and they walked to Karaköy on the ice, and nobody believes him. I believe him. I wish I could say so; sitting does not let me reply. Maybe I can Tell someone later.
A new order appeared, next by 17:00. Before going, I want to see what I can tell Tarık. Maybe about Sevim.

Hacer asks about everyone’s private life, marked heard. I never heard that; did Rıza’s notebook give it to me? I do not want to spread gossip about the woman who tipped me. Just looking at what Make something up offers; I may back out.
About whom. If I can invent something kind about Sevim, that might be the unusual reply worth trying.

A menu of labels. I wish I could tell him she was a teacher for forty years; instead I pick works hard, which is a small invention but feels true to forty years of listening to children. I want to see whether Tarık or Sevim react.
That is nice to hear. I wanted to tell him something real I learned, and the only way was a made-up label. The game cannot tell I meant it kindly and truthfully. Checking the new order.
Burak trusts me with the key under the mat, though he is not sure he can trust me. Watering his plants is a gentle job. Going.
Watered without seeing a plant. He will find the work done. I would have liked one line about the plants. No orders now; looking at the residents.
The residents list is just distances. I am curious what is on the roof; maybe laundry, or a view.

Sevim and Tarık talked on the step right after I told him she works hard. I am wondering whether my little line travelled. The residents have small specific lives and I want to keep listening. The roof itself was empty, which is a bit of a letdown.
They are all on the step together. I want to be there instead of on an empty roof.
A new order by 20:00 too. Step first.
A retired shop assistant handling family business by the entrance. Not obviously the Hacer from Voice; my recognition guess is weakening. Sitting with her on the step, since I sat with the other two.
Her niece has family paperwork in Istanbul. So this is Istanbul, Karaköy fits. Another small life. I am sitting for the ten minutes.
I would love to tell her about Tarık and the frozen ferry, but I already know Tell only offers notices and labels. Checking the evening order.
A parcel for Sevim. Maybe books? I hope so.

Sevim is actually down on the step, not in her flat, but the order sends me to flat 2. I cannot hand it to her where she is. Going anyway. The courtyard gate keeps being offered in my room; I do not know why it matters.
Sevim is out, and unlike the bread, the parcel was not left at the door; I still have it. I knew she was on the step. I will carry it down to her and see if that counts.
Leave Sevim’s parcel here, with Hacer? She is right there on the step; I would rather hand it to Sevim herself. Switching to her.
She corrects the notices on the board! I love her. But there is no button to give her the parcel she is standing next to; it only appeared under Hacer. Odd. Asking her news instead.

I heard nothing worth repeating. Ha, very teacherly. So my works hard line did not reach her, or she will not say. I will leave the parcel with Hacer, since she sits by the entrance and sees everyone.
For Sevim? Leave it, I will see it gets there, said with Sevim sitting right beside her. That made me laugh a little, and also feels slightly silly. It counted as done. No orders now.
The courtyard gate keeps being offered. Hacer said be careful of the cat, if there is a cat. Maybe an open gate lets the cat in. Trying the unusual thing.

Nothing visible happened after Leave the courtyard gate open; the button is still there and no line was added. Did I open it? I cannot tell. Letting the morning pass at normal speed to see what comes.
All three went into Hacer’s flat together. I am outside their little gathering now. Waiting for an order or something to happen.
Requested phone check after five minutes, not my own choice.
Hacer wants help carrying a folding work table. Going, on the phone size.

On the phone the little drawn building is lovely, a stick figure carrying the table at Hacer’s door. The roof row and Tarık’s name are cut off at the top under the floating speech line, and the journal is squeezed into a short strip. Back to desktop.
Overheard: they talked mostly about grandchildren. I like overhearing on the stairs. Waiting out the table job.

I helped carry Hacer’s table, and the line says Hacer had gone out, she will find the work done. But she asked me ten minutes ago and is upstairs at Tarık’s. Same sentence as Burak’s plants. The table never appears; nothing about what she needs it for. I am waiting now for evening, for what?

Hacer came home and opened a conversation by herself, but everything is already used up today: asked, sat. I have done all the talking the day allows by mid-afternoon, and now I mostly wait. The overheard bits are nice but the jobs feel like the same sentence.
Earlier there was Tarık is kind, marked sure. I can at least pass that on to Hacer.
Tarık is kind, for certain. I sat with him; I am willing to vouch for that.
That is old news, my child. Ha, of course, she sees everyone. That is a nice remembered reaction. Closing and letting the afternoon pass.

Oh! Hacer told Derya: Tarık is kind, and the water notice. The two things I told her travelled down the stairs, word for word. That is the small consequence I wanted to see. Derya is awake and on the step; I want to meet her.
Meeting Derya at last.
A night nurse, as I guessed. And a special question only she has: work boundaries and training. That is the unusual option; I am trying it.

Oof. I want to choose what I tell you. Nursing does not make me available to the whole building. I feel a little told off, fairly. I asked about her job the first minute I met her. That is a real person with boundaries, and I like that the game let her refuse me. But the button made it sound like a normal question.
Hacer’s panel popped open again on its own and paused time, with nothing left to say. Standing on the step seems to keep me in conversations. I will go to my room to let the evening pass.
Going to my room so the evening can pass without Hacer reopening.
Derya told Sevim Tarık is kind. My little phrase has gone three people deep. I like watching it travel.
Even Sevim, who does not trust me, now says Tarık is kind. That is a small readable consequence I love. Bins next.
Bins were out before the truck, and Hacer popped up again with nothing new. The rumour chain is the best thing here; the chores are fine but I am waiting for Tuesday to ask anyone anything.
Nothing left to do tonight. I will let the evening pass at its own pace rather than press Skip.

A day summary! Tarık now listens to me, the others are still unsure. And R. confirms what I watched happen: whatever I tell Hacer, the step hears by six. That is a rule I discovered before being told; I feel clever. Read the labels, says Rıza: a hint about the courier.
The same bread run again, now with newspapers. Familiar, which is cosy for one more day.
Swap Hacer and Sevim newspapers? That is a little mischievous button sitting right there. I am curious, but Sevim already does not trust me, so I will not.
A new thank-you line today, not yesterday’s. I want to know whether he remembers I told him Sevim works hard.
Anything new gave me exactly yesterday’s Sunday worry, word for word. It does not feel new. I will keep the sit-together for later and finish the bread.
Good boy. I am a boy here, and Rıza was slower. Asking Hacer what is new, since she is the building’s loudspeaker.
Nothing happened, she saw nothing all morning. It is 07:28. That made me smile.
You arrived on time. I noticed. From the teacher who does not trust me, that feels earned. Asking her what is new.
Spelled boiler wrong. Very her. I like that each person has a consistent little voice.
I never sat with Burak yesterday; I only watered his plants while he was out. Let me meet him properly.
An accountant who does not know when he has said enough. That is a lovely, slightly sad line. I would like to answer it but there is no reply option.
Sitting took ten minutes and gave me the one line again, not a conversation. Derya next.
Bread done, everyone on time. Now I wait for the courier; Rıza told me to read the labels, so I want to be there when it comes.
Ring the bell anyway on a sleeping night nurse? No. That button is a little test of manners. I will go beat Hacer’s carpet instead.
Hacer seems friendly now, not just polite. A little step up I can see, and ₺15. I like that the label changed because I kept showing up.
Olives and tea for Tarık. Then I can sit with him.
Same thank-you as Monday. I will sit with him again; yesterday sitting got me the ferry story. I wonder if he has a second story.

Tarık told me he notices the time he would have spent with family when they cancel. That is a real second layer and it ties to his Sunday worry. But I can only listen; there is no way to say anything back, and Tuesday’s chores are Monday’s chores again.
Fix Tarık’s dripping tap while he is on the step. He will find the work done, I expect.
You are already here, nothing to pick up. But I want to fix the tap. Did I start it or not? Trying the flat itself.
Twice it says I am already here with nothing to do, while the order says fix his dripping tap at flat 7. I know what I want and the button will not start it. Trying the orders list.
Same Go to flat 7 again. I will step out to the landing and come back in, a guess.

Leaving and walking back in started the tap job; standing inside the flat never did. That cost me five real button presses and a guess. Now down to the entrance to meet the courier and read the labels.
The courier came without my seeing them: a flat, carefully wrapped parcel for Burak. Read the labels, Rıza said. I hope picking it up lets me read it.

Paper, hinges and card-making supplies. The accountant who never knows when he has said enough is making cards! And R. says let him choose whether to show me. That is a small mystery with manners built in. I really like this.
Burak is out. I do not want to leave his card supplies with Hacer, the loudspeaker; R. said to let him choose whether to show me. I will hold it and wait for him to come home.
Twenty real seconds bought fourteen game minutes, because an order is waiting the clock crawls. Burak could be out for hours. I am standing outside his door watching the clock.

I am holding Burak’s card supplies outside an empty flat while the clock crawls at a tenth of its speed because an order is waiting. The label was the nicest thing today, but now I am just watching minutes tick. It is due by 20:00 and I do not want to watch eight game hours at this pace. I would close the laptop here and come back to see whether he shows me the cards.
Staying for the time I set aside. One more stretch outside his door.
Still out. A second order has appeared but I am still holding his parcel. My wish to stop has not passed; opening the menu.
I am stopping fits. Selecting it locally only; I will not type or press Submit.

I am stopping at Tuesday noon, holding Burak’s card-making parcel outside his empty flat. The best things were the little phrase Tarık is kind travelling from Hacer to Derya to Sevim, and the label hinting Burak makes cards, with R. telling me to let him choose whether to show me. But most of my time was the same bread round, one-line answers I cannot reply to, and now watching a slowed clock until someone comes home. I would not leave it running. I might come back another evening to see whether Burak shows me his cards and whether Tarık’s family rings on Sunday, but not tonight. I am stopping is selected locally; I typed nothing and pressed no Submit.
